Upwanshi and Shri Parth Dixit, Advocates f Shri Naval Kishor Gupta, Public Prosecutor for respo Shri Ravi Rahul, Advocate for respondent no.2.. Order
texts.facts: This application, under S.482 of Cr.P.C./528 of BNSS has been filed seeking quashment of FIR in Crime No. 06/2024 registered at Police Station Vidisha Mahila Police Thana, Vidisha for offences under sections 498A, 294, 323, 506 and 34 of IPC and Ss. 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. 2. Applicant No.1 is husband, applicant No.2 is mother-in-law and applicant no.3 is father-in-law of respondent No.2. 3. Prosecution case, in short, is that respondent No.2 lodged an FIR alleging that on 14/11/2023 on the issue of bringing less dowry, she was beaten by applicants and was abused filthily and also extended a threat that she would be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:3846 burnt alive. Accordingly, she called her brother and came to her parental home on 15/11/2023 and the entire incident was narrated by her. It was further alleged that she got married to applicant No.1 on 30/5/2023 in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals. In dowry, a two-wheeler vehicle, apart from gold and silver ornamnets and other house hold articles were given as per the demand raised by the applicants. Although, a cash amount of Rs.1,80,000/- was also given, but applicants picked-up a Virendra Singh Sumali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56620400/ 1 quarrel during marriage ceremonies on the ground of less cash amount. However, the matter was somehow pacified. It was alleged that on earlier occasions also, she was ousted from her matrimonial house on the ground that applicant No.1 is in service and sufficient dowry has not been given as per his status. Even in the reconcilliation proceedings, applicant No.1 had refused to take her back. 4. Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No.2, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that since the allegations are vague, general and omnibus in nature, therefore, FIR is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. It is further submitted that respondent No.2 has turned hostile during her cross-examination. 5. Heard, learned counsel for applicants. 6. So far as submission that respondent No.2 has turned hostile is concerned, the said submission is misconceived and false even to the knowledge of applicants. Counsel for applicant has provided copy of examination-in-chief of respondent No.2. It appears that respondent No.2 forgot certain aspects and as Public Prosecutor is not authorized to put leading questions to respondent No.2 , therefore, she was declared hostile, but during cross-examination by the Public Prosecutor, she narrated the allegations against the applicants. Therefore, it cannot be said that respondent No.2 has turned hostile. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:3846 7.
texts.arguments: The Supreme Court in the case of Taramani Parakh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260 has held as under: "12. In Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P. (2014) 16 SCC 551, it was observed (SCC p. 553, paras 8-9): "8. In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662]it was observed (SCC p. 217, para 5): "5. ... A tendency has, however, developed for roping in all relations of the in-laws of the deceased wives in the matters of dowry deaths which, if not discouraged, is likely to affect the case of the prosecution even against the real culprits. In their overenthusiasm and anxiety to seek conviction for maximum people, the parents of the deceased have been found to be making efforts for involving other relations which ultimately weaken the case of the prosecution even against the real accused as appears to have happened in the instant case." Virendra Singh Sumali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56620400/ 2 Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations, unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations. Reference may be made to K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar, (2000) 8 SCC 547 : 2001 SCC (Cri) 27, Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate, (1998) 5 SCC 749 : 1998 SCC (Cri) 1400, State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 : 1992 SCC (Cri) 426 : AIR 1992 SC 604 and Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P., (2011) 11 SCC 259 : (2011) 3 SCC (Cri) 159." 13. The question whether the appellant has in fact been Virendra Singh Sumali vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56620400/ 3 harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out. Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible." 9. The Supreme Court in the case of Rupali Devi v. State of U.P., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384 has held as under:- "14. "Cruelty" which is the crux of the offence under Section 498-A IPC is defined in Black's Law Dictionary to mean "the intentional and malicious infliction of mental or physical suffering on a living creature, esp. a human; abusive treatment; outrage (abuse, inhuman treatment, indignity)". Cruelty can be both physical or mental cruelty. The impact on the mental health of the wife by overt acts on the part of the husband or his relatives; the mental stress and trauma of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:3846 being driven away from the matrimonial home and her helplessness to go back to the same home for fear of being ill-treated are aspects that cannot be ignored while understanding the meaning of the expression "cruelty" appearing in Section 498-A of the Penal Code. The emotional distress or psychological effect on the wife, if not the physical injury, is bound to continue to traumatise the wife even after she leaves the matrimonial home and takes shelter at the parental home. Even if the acts of physical cruelty committed in the matrimonial house may have ceased and such acts do not occur at the parental home, there can be no doubt that the mental trauma and the psychological distress caused by the acts of the husband including verbal exchanges, if any, that had compelled the wife to leave the matrimonial home and take shelter with her parents would continue to persist at the parental home. Mental cruelty borne out of physical cruelty or abusive and humiliating verbal exchanges would continue in the parental home even though there may not be any overt act of physical cruelty at such place." 10. This Court in the case of Amar Singh vs. Smt. Vimla decided on 22.06.2021 in Criminal Revision No.2376/2020 (Gwalior Bench) has held that compelling a married woman to live in her parental home amounts to cruelty. 11. Even in reconciliation proceedings, respondent No.2 had alleged that she was beaten and harassed physically by her husband and she has been ousted. The Supreme Court in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Private Limited Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in (2021) 19 SCC 401 has held as under:- "13. From the aforesaid decisions of this Court, right from the decision of the Privy Council in Khwaja Nazir Ahmad [King Emperor v. Khwaja Nazir Ahmad, 1944 SCC OnLine PC 29: (1943- 44) 71 203: AIR 1945 PC 18], the following principles of law emerge: 13.1. Police has the statutory right and duty under the relevant provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure contained in Chapter XIV of the Code to investigate into cognizable offences. 13.2. Courts would not thwart any investigation into the cognizable offences. 13.4. The power of quashing should be exercised sparingly with circumspection, in the "rarest of rare cases". Kapur [R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab, 1960 SCC NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:3846 OnLine SC 21: AIR 1960 SC 866] and Bhajan Lal [State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335: 1992 SCC (Cri) 426], has the jurisdiction to quash the FIR/complaint. In the light of judgments passed by the Supreme Court in the cases of XYZ v. Akram Siddiqui v. State of Bihar reported in (2019) 13 SCC 350, State of A.P. v. Gourishetty Mahesh reported in (2010) 11 SCC 226, M. Srikanth v. State of Telangana, reported in (2019) 10 SCC 373, CBI v. Arvind Khanna reported in (2019) 10 SCC 686, State of MP Vs. Kunwar Singh by order dated 30.06.2021 passed in Cr.A. No.709/2021, Munshiram v.
